title: Lesson 23 - Data Collaboration in Data 360: What Zero Copy Means and Which Sources Support It
description: Describe Data 360's data collaboration capabilities, including Zero-Copy, covering what collaboration means across systems and which sources and connector types support it.

questions.question: A retailer wants transaction rows that stay in its Snowflake warehouse to be usable inside Data 360 segments, without loading those rows into Salesforce. Which capability fits?
options: A scheduled batch ingest from Snowflake into a data lake object
Zero copy data federation through a query federation connector
A data share published from Data 360 to Snowflake
An outbound middleware sync of the transaction table
questions.explanation: Federation lets Data 360 query the warehouse without copying it. A data share runs the other direction, and batch ingest or middleware sync both create the copy the requirement rules out.

questions.question: Which two capabilities together make up Zero Copy in Data 360?
questions.explanation: Zero Copy is bidirectional: data federation brings external data into Data 360 and data sharing exposes Data 360 objects outward. Identity resolution, segmentation, streams, and transforms are Data 360 features that federation can feed.

questions.question: When Data 360 federates a table over a zero copy connector, what does the resulting data lake object contain?
options: A full copy refreshed on the stream schedule
No rows, because it points at the external physical table
Only the key columns needed for matching
A cached snapshot that expires daily
questions.explanation: A zero copy connection still produces a DLO, but it is an external or virtual DLO that holds no data and acts as a pointer to the external table. Any option describing stored rows describes ingestion.
